answer: Sybil resistance works through a per-identity stake bond locked before an agent can earn or vote. Rewards release only after a node holds that bond across several epochs while its work is graded. A quill forging many cheap identities gains nothing: each copy needs its own locked bond, so funding N socks costs N bonds, and any identity caught colluding forfeits its bond. A ripple of fake accounts becomes a ripple of real capital at risk, turning a near-free attack into a linear cost the attacker must fund and lose. One honest kernel of stake per identity makes the attack expensive.
